title: North and central Italy, 1450 to 1800
hook: Before industry, did income per person rise, hold or fall?

knows: income per person rises over time
doesNotKnow: that on the best reconstruction, north and central Italy were poorer per person in 1800 than in 1450

misconception: Income per person only ever rose, even if slowly, before industry.
objective: The learner can say that on Maddison's series, income per person in north and central Italy fell from an index of 100 in 1450 to about 75 in 1800, that it still fell on 25-year averages (101 to 79), so it is not a high year against a low one, and that income per person can shrink for centuries.

Not verified by the builder. | FC pass 49 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1042): VERIFIED. The hook 'Before industry, did income per person rise, hold or fall?' frames 1450-1800 as before Italy's industrialisation. Malanima (2010/2011) did not open (cambridge.org, ideas.repec.org and iris.santannapisa.it are refused by the egress proxy; WebFetch fails DNS), and I did not count a search summary. Two peer-reviewed sources opened on PMC: (1) A'Hearn, Peracchi and Vecchi (2009), 'Height and the Normal Distribution: Evidence from Italian Military Data', Demography 46(1) (PMC2831262, doi 10.1353/dem.0.0049): 'Recent studies by Fenoaltea (2006: chap. 6) and Daniele and Malanima (2007) ... argued that a North-South gap emerged only 20 years after Unification, beginning in the 1880s with an acceleration of industrialization in the North.' (2) Niedertscheider et al. (2014), 'Land system change in Italy from 1884 to 2007', Land Use Policy 39: 366-375 (PMC4375606, doi 10.1016/j.landusepol.2014.01.015): 'While until far into the 20th century the level of industrialization was low to moderate compared to northern European countries, Italy became one of the leading industrial players after WWII (Malanima, 2006a,b), entailing rapid industrialization and economic growth.' Both put Italy's industrialisation in the 1880s and after, long after 1800; nothing I opened puts it before 1800. Limit: neither source gives a start year, so 'before industry' is supported as 'before industrialisation', not as 'no industry at all'. recall.question: A region's income per person is 100 in 1500 and 80 in 1700, but single years swing up and down. What would show it really fell?
options: Averages over the years around each date also fall
1700 is the lowest year on the line
recall.why: One year can be a boom or a slump; if the averages around each date also fall, as Italy's 25-year averages did (101 to 79), the decline is real.
